key_insight: The paper shows that block-diagonal factors interleaved with fixed permutations can be given a useful Riemannian manifold structure, enabling efficient optimization of low-parametric orthogonal matrices.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to build and train structured orthogonal layers or adapters with fewer parameters and lower memory cost, including large language model fine-tuning.
method: Characterize when the structured matrix family is a smooth manifold.
Derive Riemannian tools for orthogonal two-factor matrices.
Implement efficient optimization with automatic differentiation, parameter sharing, and no explicit dense matrix construction.
evidence_signal: The proposed algorithms are evaluated on best matrix approximation and parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models.
watch_item: The geometric and algorithmic framework is clearest for the two-factor orthogonal case; extending it to more factors may be less straightforward and could increase implementation complexity.
paper_title: Riemannian Structure and Optimization for a Class of Low-Parametric Orthogonal Matrices
